Chapter 1: When Life Throws a Curveball, Even the Helpers Need Help
You know, there’s a moment in everyone’s life when the ground suddenly shifts. Sometimes it’s a phone call that turns your world upside down, or maybe it’s a conversation that just doesn’t go the way you hoped. For one therapist, her world tilted on what should’ve been an ordinary day—right in the middle of a life that seemed to be moving along just fine.
She spent her days listening to heartbreak, to anxiety, holding space for other people’s pain. But out of nowhere, she found herself on the receiving end: the relationship she counted on—solid, she thought—ended without warning, leaving her stunned and completely adrift.
It’s easy to imagine that people who help others for a living must have it all figured out, right? But here’s something to remember: therapists are just as vulnerable to life’s messiness as anyone else. When the rug gets pulled out from under them, they don’t get a secret handbook for instant healing. They’re left with the same confusion, the same pain and big questions that bring so many of us to therapy in the first place.
In those first days, she tried to keep up appearances. She still went to work, listened to her clients, nodded along, offered gentle guidance. But inside, she was unraveling. The familiar tools she’d given to others—breathing exercises, reframing thoughts, finding meaning in pain—suddenly felt far away, almost unreachable. The ache of loss was raw, persistent, and it just wouldn’t let up.
Eventually, a new thought crept in: maybe it was time to sit on the other side of the room. Maybe it was time to talk to someone, herself. That decision wasn’t easy at all. There was embarrassment, a little voice that whispered, “Shouldn’t you be able to handle this on your own?” But the pain was just too heavy to carry alone.
Making that first appointment was an act of both humility and hope. She found herself sitting in a waiting room, feeling exposed, uncertain. The roles had completely reversed. Now she was the one searching for answers, longing for comfort, hoping for a way forward.
This experience became the start of a journey—one that challenged everything she thought she knew about healing, vulnerability, and the real work of therapy. It also deepened her understanding of what it truly means to be human: flawed, resilient, and always in need of connection.
